questions.question: What are dolphins, porpoises and whales called?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Cetaceans.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **__Important Points__** 

__
 
• Cetaceans are any member of an entirely aquatic group of mammals commonly known as whales, dolphins, and porpoises.
 
 
• It is commonly grouped with the **fishes.**
 
• It is distributed in all the world’s oceans from the far polar reaches to the Equator.
 
• Cetaceans have all features of mammals like breathe air, give birth to live young, **produce milk**, and have hair.
 
• Cetaceans use up to 80 percent of their lung volume in a single breath.
 
• Like all mammals Cetaceans also have a **four-chambered heart.**
 
• They reproduce by **internal fertilization.**
 
 

**​ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
• **Amphibians** are small vertebrates that can live in aquatic as well as terrestrial habitats.

 
 
• Common examples of amphibians are Bufo (Toad), Rana (Frog), Hyla (Tree frog), and Salamandra (Salamander).
 
 
 
• The odontocetes are also called as toothed whales.
 
 
• **Odontocetes** are a parvorder of cetaceans that includes dolphins, river dolphins, porpoises, pilot whales, beaked whales, and bottlenose whales,

questions.question: Which festival is celebrated to mark the birth anniversary of Prophet Muhammad?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __Milad-un-nabi.__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

__
 
• **Milad-un-nabi festival **is celebrated to mark the **birth anniversary of Prophet Muhammad.**

 
 
• This day is celebrated in the month of Rabi’ al-awwal (Third month of the Islamic calendar).
 
• It is celebrated by Muslims all over the world.
 
• It was first celebrated as an official festival in** Egypt.**
 
• On this day the followers of Prophet Muhammad will discuss and celebrate the advent of the Prophet Muhammad's birth and his teachings.
 
 
 
• Prophet Muhammad was an Arab religious and political leader.​
 
 
• Muhammed was born in Mecca.
 
• He is considered the** founder of Islam.**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] 

**Additional Information__**

 
• **Eid-ul-Fitr **is celebrating every year to acknowledge Allah’s revelation of the Quran to the Prophet Muhammad.

 
 
• It is also known as the festival of breaking fast.
 
 
 
• **Shab-e-Barat** is celebrating to commemorates the entry of Muhammad into the city of Mecca.
 
• **Eid al-Adha** is known as the festival of sacrifice.

questions.question: Which British Viceroy in India carried out the partition of Bengal?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**​Lord Curzon**__.

__
 
• Bengal was partitioned by the British viceroy **Lord Curzon.**

 
 
• Lord Curzon announced the partition of Bengal on **20th July 1905.**
 
• The partition came into effect on **16th October 1905.**
 
• At that time of partition, Bengal was the biggest province of British India that included Bihar and parts of Orissa.
 
• The British argued that the division was for administrative convenience.
 
• The partition of the Bengal is an example of the British policy of **divide and rule.**
 
• The main reason for the partition of Bengal was to destroy the political influence of the educated middle class among whom the Bengali intelligentsia was the most prominent.
 
• The **swadeshi movement **was started to protest against the partition of Bengal.
 
• Bengal partition was finally cancelled by **Lord Hardinge **in 1911.
 
 

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

• **Lord Canning** was the first viceroy and the last governor-general of India.
 
• **Lord Dalhousie** was the Governor-General of India who started the first railway line in India in 1853(connecting Bombay to Thane).

questions.question: With which Mughal ruler is the Moti Masjid in Agra associated?

__
 
• The **Moti Masjid in Agra** was built by Mughal ruler Shah Jahan.

 
 
• It is located in Agra in Uttar Pradesh.
 
• Shah Jahan constructed the Moti Masjid for his members of the royal court.

• Taj Mahal.
 
• Red Fort.
 
• Jama Masjid.
 
• Shalimar Garden in Lahore.

• Shah Jahan was imprisoned by his son** Aurangzeb** in 1658 in Agra.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

Mughals:

 
• The Mughals were descendants of two great lineages of rulers.
 
• From their mother’s side, they were descendants of Genghis Khan (died 1227), the Mongol ruler who ruled over parts of China and Central Asia.
 
• From their father’s side, they were the successors of Timur (died 1404), the ruler of Iran, Iraq and modern-day Turkey.
 
• However, the Mughals did not like to be called Mughal or Mongol. This was because Genghis Khan’s memory was associated with the massacre of innumerable people.
 
• It was also linked with the Uzbeks, their Mongol competitors.
 
• On the other hand, the Mughals were proud of their Timurid ancestry, not least of all because their great ancestor had captured Delhi in 1398.

questions.question: What is the child sex ratio?

options.text: Number of males per thousand females in the age group 0-15
Number of females per thousand males in the age group 0-6
Number of females per hundred males in the age group 0-6
Number of females per hundred males in the age group 0-15

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Number of females per thousand males in the age group 0-6.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **__Important Points__**

 
• The child sex ratio is the number of females per thousand males in the age** group 0-6.**

 
 
• The age-specific sex ratios in India started to be computed in **1961.**
 
• The child sex ratio in 2011 is decreased by **13 points.**
 
• The child sex ratio of India is **919** in the census 2011.
 
• **Haryana** is the worst state with an incredibly low child sex ratio of 793.
 
• The highest child sex ratio of 972 is found in **Arunachal Pradesh.**
 
 
 
• The sex ratio is an important indicator of gender balance in the population.

questions.question: ‘Double coincidence of wants’ is a feature of which system?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Barter system.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **__Important Points__** 

__
 
• The **barter system** is a trade in which goods are exchanged between the buyer and seller without the use of real money.

 
 
• ‘**Double coincidence of wants** is a feature of the barter system.

 
 
• Double coincidence of wants occurs when two people have goods and they are both happy to swap in exchange.
 
• People have to swap their goods in the barter system.
 
• The double coincidence of wants is the foundation of a bartering economy.
 
• Lack of double coincidence of wants is a major issue in the barter system.
 
 
 
• It is difficult to carry forward one’s wealth under the barter system.
 
• Wealth can not be stored in the form of money for future use in the barter system.
 
• The barter system is considered as the **oldest form of commerce.**
 
 

**​ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
• **Liquidity** is the measure of the cash and other assets that have available to quickly pay bills.
 
• **Forex Rate**(also called foreign exchange rate) is the price of one currency in terms of another.

• **Ashoka** was the most famous Mauryan ruler and he was the first ruler who tried to take his message to the people through inscriptions.
 
• Mauryan empire started declining due to the invasions, defections by southern princes after the death of Ashoka.
